Paragraph:
Translation: Arjuna said: My dear Krsna, seeing my friends and relatives present before me in such a fighting spirit, I feel the limbs of my body quivering and my mouth drying up.

Purport (Excerpt): Any man who has genuine devotion to the Lord has all the good qualities... As such, Arjuna, just after seeing his kinsmen... was at once overwhelmed by compassion... And so thinking, the limbs of his body began to quiver, and his mouth became dry. He was more or less astonished to see their fighting spirit... Such symptoms in Arjuna were not due to weakness but to his softheartedness...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna's emotional overwhelm rapidly escalates into acute physical symptoms. He reports these terrifying bodily sensations to his guide, Krishna.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna articulates his physiological distress: quivering limbs and dry mouth. The purport reframes these symptoms not as cowardice, but as the natural empathetic reaction of a 'softhearted' and pious individual facing immense tragedy.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna begins to experience the initial somatic manifestations of a severe stress response, losing his physical readiness for battle.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sattvic Bhava (The natural, empathetic sensitivity of a pure-hearted person, though temporarily clouded by material context)
Bhaya (Fear manifesting physically due to anticipated loss)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The text highlights a paradox: a pure devotee possesses a soft, compassionate heart, which makes the harsh realities of material duty deeply painful. Arjuna's physical breakdown is born of a genuine spiritual sensitivity clashing violently with his necessary, destructive material duty.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Arjuna is experiencing the direct physiological consequences of severe psychological distress. The activation of his sympathetic nervous system (fight-or-flight response) is causing classic somatic symptoms of anxiety—muscle tremors (quivering) and decreased salivation (dry mouth)—as his brain processes the immense threat to his loved ones.
